Callisto Architecture

Crate map, data flow, and the invariants every change must preserve.

--- ## Invariants 1. **Safe Rust only.** `unsafe_code = "forbid"` workspace-wide. 2. **License boundary.** `callisto-model` is MIT and must never depend on an FSL-1.1-MIT crate. Every other crate is FSL-1.1-MIT. Check with `grep -H "^license" crates/*/Cargo.toml`. 3. **Format-preserving manifest edits.** `Cargo.toml` goes through `toml_edit`'s CST; `package.json` is fingerprinted for indent style and line endings before a `serde_json` (`preserve_order`) round trip. No regex or line-based edits to manifests. 4. **One file-write primitive, capability-gated.** `callisto_model::atomic::atomic_write` (`NamedTempFile` in the target's own directory, `fsync`, `persist` via `fs::rename`, then `fsync` the parent directory, and its parent when the call created it; a failed sync is returned unless the filesystem cannot sync a directory) is the only way file content is written; deletions and directory creation use `std::fs`. It takes `&ApplyPermit`, a token with a private field that only `ApplyPermit::granted_unless_dry_run(dry_run)` can construct, returning `None` on a dry run. A write path that forgets to check `--dry-run` has no permit to pass and fails to compile. 5. **System Git only.** All VCS reads and writes shell out to the user's `git` binary (`callisto_model::vcs`), so Callisto sees exactly the repository, config, and identity Git itself does. No embedded Git implementation. 6. **User-facing errors are diagnosable.** Every error surfaced to a user derives `miette::Diagnostic` with a stable code and, where the fix isn't obvious from the message, `help` text. A wrapper around another crate's error (for example `GraphError::Config`) is `#[diagnostic(transparent)]` and declares no code of its own, so the inner code reaches the user. Full list: [`docs/errors.md`](docs/errors.md). Design decisions, with the options they rejected and why: [`docs/adr/README.md`](docs/adr/README.md). ## Crate map ``` Layer 1 (leaf) callisto-model Layer 2 (I/O) callisto-manifests Layer 3 (engine) callisto-graph Layer 4 (surface) callisto-cli Dev-only callisto-fixtures ``` | Crate | License | Depends on | Purpose | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | [`callisto-model`](crates/callisto-model) | MIT | none | Domain primitives (`PackageId`, `Version`, `Severity`, `Changeset`, `PreState`), `atomic_write`, `ApplyPermit`, the `CommandRunner`/`DependencyResolver` trait seams; `format`: `.changeset/*.md` and `pre.json` parser/writer; `vcs`: `GitAccess`, every Git operation as a subprocess through `CommandRunner` | | [`callisto-manifests`](crates/callisto-manifests) | FSL-1.1-MIT | model | `Manifest` trait; format-preserving Cargo/npm/PyPI manifest editors | | [`callisto-graph`](crates/callisto-graph) | FSL-1.1-MIT | model, manifests | Dependency graph, cascade engine, version planning, release execution; `conventional`: Conventional Commit parsing and bump inference; `changelog`: Markdown changelog rendering | | [`callisto-cli`](crates/callisto-cli) | FSL-1.1-MIT | model, manifests, graph | `clap` CLI surface, `miette` diagnostic rendering | | [`callisto-fixtures`](crates/callisto-fixtures) | FSL-1.1-MIT | model (dev-only) | Multi-ecosystem test corpus and in-memory test doubles | Dependencies only point down the layers (`cli` → `graph` → `manifests` → `model`). Nothing in Layer 1–3 depends on `callisto-cli`. ## Data flow ``` Workspace::load config::load -> config::resolve callisto.toml -> ResolvedConfig ManifestWalkResolver::build discover (ProjectLocator), read manifests (Manifest), assign ids, attach platform packages, apply per-package config GroupTable::resolve bind [[fixed-group]] / [[linked-group]] members plan_version -> VersionPlan (in memory) aggregate changesets + opt-in commit inference -> severity per package run_cascade dependents (runtime, build, optional, peer; never dev), groups, pre mode -> target version per package, with its reasons version --emit-decision derives and validates the decision in memory, before apply apply_version_plan (needs ApplyPermit) CST edits -> atomic_write, changelogs consume changesets -> native lock refresh -> git staging version --emit-decision writes the decision file after successful apply release decision -> intent -> envelope -> execute_release -> receipt per operation observe provider -> adopt, or perform and confirm ``` Cycles are detected with `petgraph::algo::tarjan_scc`. Git access goes through `GitAccess` (`callisto_model::vcs`). Depth: - [`docs/architecture/identity.md`](docs/architecture/identity.md): package ids, bare-name matching, config rule specificity, workspace loading, platform packages. - [`docs/architecture/versioning.md`](docs/architecture/versioning.md): plan and apply, file-level idempotence and interrupted-command limits. - [`docs/architecture/release.md`](docs/architecture/release.md): release terms, the two routes, run envelope, observation and proof tokens, the transition table, verification tiers. - [`docs/architecture/wire-compat.md`](docs/architecture/wire-compat.md): the version each release document writes and reads, what a reader does with another, and the known gaps. ## Extension seams Four traits decouple the engine from platform I/O (`callisto-model::exec`, `callisto-model::discovery`, `callisto-manifests`, `callisto-graph::locate`): - `ProjectLocator` — enumerates workspace project roots. - `CommandRunner` — runs a subprocess. `run_with_timeout`'s default implementation ignores the timeout; the CLI's runner enforces it, so a hung publish command cannot block forever. - `Manifest` — per-ecosystem read/write. Mutations only touch the in-memory CST; nothing reaches disk until `persist(&ApplyPermit)`, so one open manifest can take several mutations before one write. - `DependencyResolver` — supplies graph nodes and edges; `ManifestWalkResolver` is the only current implementation. ## Current boundaries and planned changes `PackageId` is a flexible selector/display form; `PackageKey` is a directory locator; `ReleasePackageId` is a canonical ecosystem-qualified distribution identity. A directory can own several canonical manifests, but the current package model requires one version grammar. Registry version observations do not establish a complete Python file set or identical package bytes. Known contract failures and verification gaps are tracked in [`docs/projects/V1-FINDINGS.md`](docs/projects/V1-FINDINGS.md). The proposed canonical-identity and polyglot model is in [`docs/architecture/polyglot-v1.md`](docs/architecture/polyglot-v1.md); it is not an implemented extension seam. The existing dependency graph and release-operation DAG remain the basis of the plan. ## Not covered here - Release lifecycle, CI plan/build/execute, recovery: [`docs/releasing.md`](docs/releasing.md). - Registry authentication: [`docs/publishing.md`](docs/publishing.md). - `callisto.toml` keys: [`docs/config.md`](docs/config.md). - Diagnostic codes: [`docs/errors.md`](docs/errors.md). - Behavior, including `callisto matrix`: [`docs/specs/`](docs/specs/INDEX.md). # Package identity How the workspace names packages, why bare names match across ecosystems, and where platform packages are wired in. Behavior: [`docs/specs/workspace.json`](../specs/workspace.json). Config keys: [`docs/config.md`](../config.md). Platform ownership decision: [ADR 7](../adr/0007-platform-packages-owned-through-optional-dependencies.md). ## Terms - Dual-manifest package: one directory with several admitted canonical manifests; one graph package, one version grammar and several distribution identities. Cargo+npm is supported by the model; co-located Cargo+Python currently fails with E007 because their grammars differ, including a Maturin dynamic Python version. - Co-located platform manifest: an `os`+`cpu` `package.json` in the same directory as its owner's `Cargo.toml`. - Attached platform package: an `os`+`cpu` `package.json` in its own directory, owned via another package's `optionalDependencies`. ## `PackageId` (`crates/callisto-model/src/identity.rs`) | Form | Example | `ecosystem()` | | --- | --- | --- | | `Bare(name)` | `foo`, `@scope/foo` | `None` | | `Prefixed { ecosystem, name }` | `cargo:foo`, `npm/@scope/foo` | `Some(e)` | - `parse` treats text before the first `:` or `/` as a prefix only when `Ecosystem::from_prefix` knows it, so `@scope/foo` stays bare. - `display_name` renders a prefixed id as `ecosystem/name`. - `PackageId` is the display and selector form; `Package::key()` is the workspace-relative directory of the first canonical manifest. It survives display promotion, not a directory move. `ReleasePackageId` names each canonical distribution as `ecosystem/name` using that manifest's own native name. - Default tags use `display_name()`: `foo@{version}` while bare, `cargo/foo@{version}` after promotion. Promotion therefore also changes the namespace of newly created default tags (ADR 11). - `matches` is a weak "could be the same package" relation, not equality: - Different names never match. - A bare id matches any id with the same name, in either direction: bare is an ecosystem wildcard. - Two prefixed ids match only when their ecosystems are equal. - A dual-manifest package can have different native names. `IdentityIndex` resolves each ecosystem/name to its owner; the weak `matches` relation alone does not establish distribution identity or ownership. ## Resolving ambiguity A workspace can hold `cargo:foo` and `npm:foo` as separate packages; ambiguity is resolved where a lookup happens. Qualified selectors work before and after promotion. Canonical-only new references are planned in [the v1 design](polyglot-v1.md), not implemented by today's parser. - `aggregate::resolve_target_package` resolves changeset entries through `IdentityIndex::resolve_id`, which maps qualified native distribution names to their owner and rejects ambiguous bare names. `status` attributes changeset entries and checks their well-formedness through the same resolver. `PackageId::resolve_unique` scans display ids, is deprecated, and is not equivalent for dual-manifest packages with different native names. - `[[package]]` rules use `config::resolve::resolve_package_config`: two linear passes over the rules in declaration order, prefixed rules first, then bare. It never sorts the rules. A bare rule that reaches a promoted name is an `AmbiguousName` error, using `ResolvedConfig::promoted_siblings`. - `[[package-set]]` is a fallback applied in `ManifestWalkResolver::build` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/walk.rs`) only when no `[[package]]` rule matched. Patterns (`config/pattern.rs`) are globs over the name with an optional ecosystem prefix, tested against every ecosystem the package has a manifest in. ## Loading a workspace `Workspace::load` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/lib.rs`): 1. `config::load` reads `callisto.toml` (absent means empty) and calls `config::resolve`, which does all validation and defaulting. Callers holding a `RawConfig` in memory call `resolve` directly. 2. `ManifestWalkResolver::build` discovers projects, assigns ids (`IdentityIndex`), attaches platform packages and applies per-package config. 3. `GroupTable::resolve` binds group members to ids, then names promoted into several ecosystems are recorded as `promoted_siblings`. 4. The tag index is built lazily, on the first `Workspace::tags` call. A Cargo package inherits from the Cargo workspace that governs it, found the way Cargo finds it (`cargo::enclosing_workspace_manifest`): `package.workspace`, else the nearest manifest at or above the package with a `workspace` table, never above the workspace root. That workspace can be below the root, so the walk, the version guard, release-commit verification, lockfile refresh and `registry_argv` all resolve it per package. Cargo does not judge membership for inheritance, and neither does this lookup: a root that excludes or omits the package is a repository Cargo itself rejects. `Workspace::load` returns only a complete workspace, and it is the only way to get one. Every manifest the walk cannot open (for its platform role, publish targets or dependencies) is recorded as an error-level `ManifestUnresolved` diagnostic, and `load` turns any of them into E313 naming each manifest once, so no command sees a roster smaller than the repository. ## Historical ownership For a promoted package, `TagIndex::build` also considers bare-name tags. `history::sole_owner_at` picks the same-named candidate whose first canonical manifest path exists at the tag's commit. When none does, because the directory moved or the package gained a higher-priority manifest, it asks which ecosystems had a manifest declaring the shared name at that commit, found with `git grep` and confirmed by reading only the matching manifests. The owner is the one candidate whose own manifest in such an ecosystem has that native name today, taken from the identity index. Two or more matches, or none, mean no owner. `assign_promoted_pre_keys` applies the same check at the commit that added `pre.json`, and E245 reports a baseline with no unique owner. A demoted package, whose same-named sibling was removed, also considers the qualified tags of its first manifest's ecosystem and keeps the newest version across both families. A rename that changes the native name, or a move that changes it too, leaves no evidence in Git. Declare it with `previous-tag-templates`; do not infer it from the directory key. ## Platform packages in code | Step | Where | | --- | --- | | Find candidates outside the npm workspace globs | `ProjectLocator::projects_and_platform_candidates` | | Attach a platform to its single owner, or warn | `platform_owners` in `walk.rs` | | Look up a platform's owner by the platform's own npm name | `IdentityIndex::platform` | | List an owner's attached platforms (co-located ones excluded) | `IdentityIndex::attached_platforms` | | Write the owner's version into platform manifests and pin `optionalDependencies` | `platform_version_writes` in `commands/version.rs` (version and snapshot) | | Publish each platform before its owner | `commands/release/derive.rs`: one `PlatformPublish` operation per attached platform | - A `PlatformPublish` operation carries the owner's package id and version, so it passes the intent's check that every operation belongs to a decision entry, and each one is a prerequisite of the owner's npm `RegistryPublish`. - It gets no tag, forge or artifact operation of its own; it publishes by directory. - Release identities come from `release_package_ids` (`commands/release_decision.rs`): one per canonical manifest, using that manifest's own name, so a dual-manifest package with different Cargo and npm names releases under both. # Release execution The types that make a release run safe to crash and rerun, and how the two release routes share them. Behavior: [`docs/specs/release.json`](../specs/release.json). Operator guide: [`docs/releasing.md`](../releasing.md). Decisions: ADRs [2](../adr/0002-committed-decision-is-release-authority.md), [3](../adr/0003-reruns-adopt-landed-effects.md), [4](../adr/0004-ecosystem-tools-publish-and-own-auth.md) and [7](../adr/0007-platform-packages-owned-through-optional-dependencies.md). ## Terms - Package: a dependency-graph node owned by a directory; it can expose several canonical manifest/distribution identities. - Distribution identity: `ReleasePackageId`, an ecosystem-qualified native package name. A graph package with several identities has one tag, one forge release and one forge publish, each carried by the package's owner: its first selected identity in manifest order (Cargo, then npm, then PyPI). - Artifact: the bytes of one *(package, version, target)*, declared by `[[release.artifact]]`. It has no version, tag or changelog of its own. Callisto does not parse `target`; CI supplies product-slot bytes and Callisto records where they go. Registry publishing can invoke native build/pack tools, including Python's build backend. - Product package: `[release].product-package`. Every artifact slot uploads to the product's one GitHub Release, even when another package built the bytes (`ArtifactSlotId.package`). - Decision: the package and version roster (`ReleaseDecisionV1`). - Intent: the decision plus the source snapshot, every operation with its prerequisites, and the artifact slots, sealed by a digest (`ReleaseIntentV1`). - Operation: one effect on one provider, identified by package, version and role: registry publish, platform publish, tag, forge release (draft), artifact upload, forge publish. ## Layers | Layer | Crate | Contents | | --- | --- | --- | | Authorities | `callisto-model` (MIT) | Run envelope and execution state (`release/execution.rs`), observations and evidence (`release_observation.rs`), transition table (`release_transition.rs`) | | Derivation and execution | `callisto-graph` | Decisions (`commands/release_decision.rs`), intent derivation (`commands/release/derive.rs`), local route (`commands/release/local.rs`), executor (`commands/release_execution.rs`), provider adapters (`commands/release/provider/`) | | Entry points | `callisto-cli` | `commands/release.rs`: `release`, `release plan`, `release build-python`, `release artifact-manifest`, `release execute` | ## Two routes, one executor ``` local: derive_release_roster (untagged versions, plus tagged-on-HEAD releases not fully observed) -> plan_local_release -> intent CI: committed decision file, or --package over plan_version -> release plan -> intent -> build -> release execute both: intent -> ReleaseRunEnvelopeV1::new -> execute_release -> ReleaseReceiptV1::from_state ``` - `plan_local_release` is the one derivation behind both `callisto release --dry-run` and the real run. - A tag proves only that the tag was created. `incomplete_tagged_releases` observes every operation of the packages tagged on HEAD and keeps any not exactly satisfied; a tag on another commit is never observed. - `ci_release_route` sends a workspace with artifact slots or platform builds to the CI route before anything runs. - `expand_selection` (group members) and `require_dependencies_selected` (unselected unreleased dependencies) apply to both routes. ## Managed release PR and workflow Callisto's own [release workflow](../../.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml) reconstructs one `callisto/version-packages` PR from `main` when changesets land. It versions manifests and changelogs; merging the PR consumes the changesets on `main` and authorizes publication. - The action commits non-workflow changes through `createCommitOnBranch`, then moves the release ref through REST. It does not run a local `git push`. Workflow files remain unchanged, so the built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN` needs no workflow-write permission. - Commits are GitHub-signed as `github-actions[bot]`. An App or fine-grained token can use another identity. - Branch protection must require reviews and CI checks. CODEOWNERS alone does not enforce review. - `version-pr` maintains the PR; `release` runs the local release route. Artifact and platform packages use plan/build/execute. Deprecated `publish` and `create_github_release` action inputs are ignored. The [action manifest](../../.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml) defines current inputs and outputs. - Only `execute` receives registry credentials. Plan and build jobs receive none. Temporary intent, receipt, artifacts, and build output live under `RUNNER_TEMP`, outside the checkout. GitHub Actions schedules jobs, transports artifacts, and injects credentials. Callisto validates source, provenance, plan, observations, transitions, terminality, receipts, and artifacts. Workflow shell must not reimplement those semantics. Recovery dispatch uses current orchestration on `main` with an explicit merged source SHA and runs credential-free `recovery-checks` instead of full `verify`. The generated release action maps credentials without changing owner-defined publish hooks: - npm: copy existing user config to a mode-0600 temporary file, add an npmjs entry interpolating `NPM_TOKEN`, point npm-compatible tools at it, and remove it on exit. The original config is unchanged. `NPM_TOKEN` remains available for native hooks and `.npmrc` interpolation. Custom registries use native configuration. - Bun: also set `NPM_CONFIG_TOKEN`, because Bun does not honor `NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG`. - PyPI: map `PYPI_TOKEN` to `TWINE_USERNAME=__token__` and `TWINE_PASSWORD` for upload. The build backend receives no registry or forge credentials. - Cargo: pass `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` through to Cargo. ## Run envelope and state (`release/execution.rs`) - `ReleaseRunEnvelopeV1` is one run's identity: orchestration revision, release-source revision, intent digest, artifact-manifest digest. - `ReleaseRunEnvelopeV1::new` is its only constructor. The source revision and intent digest are read from the intent, so a caller cannot assert them; the constructor cross-checks the rest against the intent before any effect. - `ReleaseExecutionStateV1::new(intent, envelope)` is the only way to start a state, so no state exists without a validated envelope. - The state is never persisted or loaded. Every run starts with every operation `Pending`. - `ReleaseReceiptV1::from_state` builds the receipt from the state alone: the envelope plus the evidence each operation recorded on success. Nothing re-observes providers after the effects. ## Observation and evidence (`release_observation.rs`) - `ProviderObservationV1` is `Absent`, `Exact { evidence }`, `Conflict { reason }` or `Indeterminate { cause }`. Reasons and causes are closed enums. - `ProviderEvidenceV1` is closed and per role: registry version, git tag peeled commit, forge release tag and draft flag, artifact size and sha256. - `ReleaseOperationObservationV1::new` rejects evidence whose shape does not belong to the operation's role; deserialization goes through it too. - Proof tokens: `AbsentProof` is minted only from `Absent`, `ExactEvidence` only from `Exact`. - `execute_release` observes each operation once before its effect: exact is adopted, absent is performed then confirmed, anything else stops the run before the effect. Provider reads use native tools for Cargo and npm, and `curl` for PyPI's PEP 691 JSON simple index: - Cargo: `cargo info NAME@VERSION --registry REGISTRY` runs from the source root. Matching `version:` means exact; exit 101 with ``could not find `NAME@VERSION` `` means absent. Other results are indeterminate. Yanked versions are invisible to `cargo info`; a rejected publish ends without a receipt. - npm: `npm view NAME@VERSION version --json`. - PyPI: a matching file means exact; 404 or no match means absent; transport failure or non-JSON means indeterminate. Yanked matches count as absent. Before an effect, `release execute` also builds the release's files once into a temporary directory and compares their names with the index, so a partly uploaded release uploads only what is missing and is satisfied only when the whole set is there. These reads are version-level checks, not proof of identical bytes or the npm dist-tag. Registry endpoints must be HTTPS. Read-only observations retry 429, 5xx, rate-limited 403, and transport failures with backoff and `Retry-After`. Effects are never blindly retried; outbound commands have deadlines. ## Transition table (`release_transition.rs`) `transition` is the only function that computes an `OperationState`; `ReleaseExecutionStateV1::apply` is the only mutator. The whole legal edge set: | From | Event | To | | --- | --- | --- | | Pending | `Attempt { AbsentProof }` | Attempting | | Pending | `ObservedExactBeforeEffect { ExactEvidence }` | AlreadySatisfied | | Attempting | `Confirmed { ExactEvidence }` | Published | | Attempting | `EffectFailedAndAbsent { AbsentProof }` | Failed | | Pending or Attempting | `Blocked { reason }` | Blocked | - Any other pair is an `InvalidTransition`. - `Attempting` is unreachable without a proof of absence. - `Published` (our effect landed) stays distinct from `AlreadySatisfied` (it existed before this run). ## Forge ordering - A GitHub release is created as a draft, assets upload to the draft, and publication is a separate last operation that depends on every upload. A published release can be immutable and refuse new assets. - GitHub's release-by-tag endpoint omits drafts, so the forge lookup finds the release ID by tag through GraphQL, then reads the release by ID (`release/github.rs`). - GitHub's reads lag its writes by seconds. The check right after this run's own create, upload or publish retries an absent answer for about a minute before it reports a conflict (`observe_until_visible`). The tag/announcement barrier covers all required publications of a graph package: a package's tag waits for the registry publishes of every release identity it has (`OpIndex::tag_prerequisites`), so a dual Cargo/npm owner's one tag and public release follow both publishes, in no fixed ecosystem order. Selecting one identity of a dual package makes that identity the owner, so the tag waits only for the selected publishes. An intent derived before this rule fails closed as stale and is rebuilt with `release plan`. See [the scoped design](polyglot-v1.md) for proposed ownership and future Go tag-publication semantics. ## Wire and observation boundaries Stdout JSON reports include `schemaVersion`, `command` and `dryRun`; durable decision, intent, artifact-manifest and receipt files retain their own wire shapes. The CLI's `release-pr verify` reader accepts both the strict bare decision and unchanged decide report, validating the report metadata before passing the payload to the shared domain constructor. Unknown and duplicate fields remain errors; durable wire readers are unchanged. The real-binary action contract exercises this producer/consumer boundary through inline, file and stdin inputs. Managed PR verification compares the original snapshot before staging and before moving the release ref. After a successful update, the action confirms the ref's exact new SHA and supplies it as `--applied-head` for the final check. The model validates the original update decision and allows only its selected PR's head to change to that SHA; the base, repository, PR roster and every other head remain unchanged. Create decisions keep strict equality until the PR is created. The action does not rewrite its decision or discard concurrency checks after its own effect. Registry evidence currently confirms a version, with optional checksum/yank fields; it does not establish byte identity. Python completion has two modes. Without a sealed file set (the local route, and a CI route whose manifest seals none) it is judged against the files the executing run builds, matched by name, and digests are compared only for files that run uploaded: a rebuild need not be byte-identical to an earlier attempt. With a sealed set, a build job (`release build-python`, no credentials) builds the files and `release artifact-manifest --seal-python` records each file's name, size and sha256 in the manifest, so the envelope's manifest digest covers them. `release execute` verifies the bytes, builds nothing, uploads those files, and treats any index file under a sealed name with another sha256 as an error (E307). The sealed sets are all or none per plan and each belongs to a Python publish of the intent; the manifest stays at schema version 1 because a manifest without sets is unchanged and an older reader rejects the new field. Artifact size/sha256 validation otherwise applies to declared GitHub assets. A PyPI registry reads its simple index at `url` and uploads to `publish-url` when set, else `url`; both endpoints are part of the registry binding. Authenticated reads and HTML-only indexes are not supported. ## Verification tiers - Fault-injection simulator (`commands/release_simulator.rs`): drives the real `execute_release` against an in-memory provider world, crashing at every provider call and injecting every provider outcome, with each rerun starting fresh. It asserts that a receipt is issued only when every effect really landed and only from state, that no landed effect is re-issued, that no effect lands before its prerequisites, and that each scenario converges within three clean reruns. - Provider contract tier: fake providers replay captured real responses from `testing/fixtures/providers/`; `TOOL_SHAPES` in `crates/callisto-cli/tests/common/release_harness.rs` rejects flags a fake does not know, and `provider_flag_contract_tests.rs` checks each emitted flag against the real tool. `just provider-fixtures` re-captures and `just provider-contract` checks shapes live; both need the network and are outside `just ci`. - Wire shapes: decision, intent, envelope and receipt each carry a `SCHEMA_VERSION`; the execution state has no wire shape. `callisto schema --type release-receipt` publishes the receipt schema, guarded by `crates/callisto-cli/tests/schema_guard_test.rs`. ## Installer and product assets `setup-callisto` defaults to `source: auto`: install the requested release, even in a Callisto checkout. An explicit `version` wins; otherwise `latest` resolves the pinned action ref to its `callisto@` release when possible. A `callisto-cli` manifest alone does not select checkout source. `source: local` builds the checkout and ignores `version`. It requires tracked root and CLI manifests, the CLI entrypoint, a Cargo-confirmed workspace member and binary target, Git, Cargo, jq, and locked offline metadata resolution. It uses the checkout's `target/` cache, installs under `RUNNER_TEMP`, and never falls back from invalid local source. Callisto's release jobs use this mode. Downloaded binaries are checked with `gh attestation verify` against `orin-dx/callisto` and the `callisto-release.yml` signer before extraction. Only the `callisto` binary is extracted. `verification: require` aborts on failure; `fallback` (default) deletes the asset and installs from crates.io; `skip` warns and uses it. Fallback pins the requested version except for `latest`. Older unattested releases motivate the default. `require` and `fallback` never run an unverified asset. Product assets target `aarch64-apple-darwin`, `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, and `x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`. Apple signing and notarization are out of scope. GitHub provenance binds assets to the orchestration revision; the intent and artifact manifest bind their bytes to the release source. Before writing a manifest (or a platform manifest), apply reads its current version: `from` means write, `to` means already done, anything else is `UnexpectedManifestVersion`. - A manifest already at `to` is still staged: the crashed run may have written it without `git add`. - Apply refreshes affected lockfiles and stages generated version state before consuming changesets or exiting `pre.json`. It stages input deletions with `git rm --cached --ignore-unmatch` before removing the files from disk, so a failed index update leaves the inputs available for recovery. A fresh command does not retain the in-memory plan and can refuse already-stable staged outputs; E121 directs the user to inspect both diffs and finish consuming retained inputs only when the staged outputs are verified. Staged metadata-only edits are allowed. During `mode: exit`, prerelease versions awaiting stable finalization remain eligible, but changed stable versions are not exempt from the retry guard. It does not restore a lost plan. Apply retains changesets and pre-state deletion inputs until lock refresh and staging of generated state succeed, then stages their removal before unlinking them from disk. A late `--emit-decision` write failure is actionable refusal, not automatic replay of an in-memory plan that no longer exists. Apply refreshes each existing lockfile for every ecosystem represented by an actual version, dependency, platform or optional-dependency write, including dual-manifest packages and workspace-root Cargo writes. Cargo lockfiles are refreshed and staged per Cargo workspace, in that workspace's directory. ## Rules

# 2. The committed version decision is the release authority

Status: Accepted (implemented in #54)

## Context

- After the release PR merges, CI must verify the merged release commit before any publish, tag or GitHub release runs (PR #54).
- Before #54 the release roster was derived from the merged commit's raw diff and understood only a direct changeset-to-package match. It rejected any release in which a `[[fixed-group]]` cascade bumped a sibling that no changeset named (PR #54; code comment on `derive_release_commit_decision`).

## Decision

`callisto version --emit-decision <path>` writes the version decision it computed (package, target version, inclusion reasons) to `<path>`. The managed release-PR action writes it to `.callisto/release-decision.json` by default (`decision_path` input) and commits it in the release PR. After merge, `release plan --from-release-commit --decision <file>` reads that decision and confirms the merged commit's diff matches it exactly, no more and no less. CI never recomputes changeset, group or cascade policy at that boundary. The verified merge is also the authorization: the release workflow has no separate approval gate (no GitHub Environment approval or required reviewers) (incident report §2, requirements 1 and 2; PR #101, "fix(release): remove Environment approval gate").

## Options considered

- **Re-derive cascade and group policy in CI after merge, or keep the raw-diff roster and teach it about groups** — rejected. "Rather than teach the re-derivation about groups -- a second, incomplete reimplementation of changeset/group/cascade resolution -- this trusts the decision `callisto version` already computed and committed … One decision surface instead of two that can drift apart" (PR #54).

## Consequences

- The released roster and versions are exactly those committed in the release PR.
- The decision file is a wire contract. Its schema is versioned: `ReleaseDecisionV1::SCHEMA_VERSION` is 2, and the reader accepts 1 and 2 so an older release PR still plans (commit 7027bbfb0).
- A decision whose entries do not match its own digest fails to decode (E166) before the diff cross-check. The digest is an unkeyed SHA-256, not a signature, so an edit with a recomputed digest that still passes the decoder's roster checks is caught only by the diff cross-check.
- A release commit that does not add or modify the decision file, consumes no changeset, whose manifest versions disagree with the decision, or that leaves a claimed package's changelog untouched is refused (E165). Nothing checks that the decision file was produced by `callisto version --emit-decision`.
- `--emit-decision` derives and validates the decision before writes, then writes its file only after apply succeeds (`crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/version.rs`). A failed apply can leave earlier manifest writes without a decision; interrupted-command recovery is tracked separately.

## Enforcement

- `crates/callisto-cli/tests/durable_release_e2e_tests.rs`: `fixed_group_cascade_bump_without_direct_changeset_is_accepted`, `release_plan_rejects_a_commit_whose_manifest_disagrees_with_its_own_decision`, `release_plan_rejects_a_hand_tampered_decision_file`.
- `derive_release_commit_decision` in `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release_decision.rs` and its unit tests (head mismatch, corrupt decision file, claimed package not observed).

## Revisit when

- Release PRs must be produced by something other than `callisto version` (for example a third-party bot) and cannot carry the decision file.
- A needed check can only be made at merge time from data the decision cannot contain.

## Sources

- PR #54 (7199ad70f), body "Why" section
- Code comment on `derive_release_commit_decision`, `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release_decision.rs`
- PR #101 (279e32361), squashed commits "fix(release): remove Environment approval gate" and "fix(release): emit the committed release decision"
- Commit 7027bbfb0 (reader accepts schema 1 and 2)
- `crates/callisto-model/src/release/decision.rs` (`decision_digest`, `ReleaseDecisionV1` deserializer)
- Incident report §2 (`git show 11038b11b^:.claude/plans/RELEASE-SELF-HOSTING-INCIDENT-2026-09-16.md`)
# 3. Reruns observe and adopt landed effects; no persisted execution state

Status: Accepted (implemented in #124)

## Context

- A release is many external effects (registry publishes, tags, GitHub releases, asset uploads). Any run can die partway.
- Owner requirements: a merged but unpublished version must be recoverable without inventing a newer version; execution must fail unless every required operation reaches a verified terminal-success state; partial publication must be safely resumable from provider state (incident report §2, requirements 4, 7, 8).
- The same report proposed durably persisted execution state (§8, SPEC-RELEASE-EXECUTION-TERMINALITY criterion 3).

## Decision

Every run observes each operation's provider state immediately before that operation's effect and adopts an effect that already landed exactly as planned (a registry version already published is adopted with a warning); anything other than exact or absent stops the run (`execute_release`, `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release_execution.rs`). Execution state lives in memory for one run. A receipt is written only when every planned operation reached verified success; an incomplete run exits non-zero. An older merged release is recovered by a fresh run that plans it with `release plan --from-release-commit <sha> --decision <path> --orchestration-revision <current sha>`, not from a state file. Callisto's own release workflow exposes this as a `release_source_sha` dispatch input; workflows generated by `callisto init` do not (`crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/init.rs` tests).

## Options considered

- **Persisted execution state file with resume** — shipped in #39, proposed again in incident report §8, removed in #124: "CI never reads execution state back (every run is a fresh runner), yet an Initial run turned an already-published registry version into E174, so 'Re-run failed jobs' could never finish a partial release" (#124).
- **Recovery commands (`release reconcile`, `release execute --recovery`, `--state`) and Initial/Recovery run kinds** — rejected with the state file in #124. Removed with them: the workspace lock, `AdoptedExact`/`RecoveredExact`, E173, E174 and the release-state schema.
- **Rerun the historical workflow run to recover** — rejected. A rerun of an old GitHub Actions run does not pick up workflow fixes merged later (incident report §2 requirement 6; §6 F-003).
- **Post-publish re-observation pass to build the receipt** — rejected: a flaky registry read could fail a release whose effects had all landed (#122, #124).

## Consequences

- A rerun ("Re-run failed jobs" or a fresh run on the release commit) finishes a partial release whose remaining operations can now succeed; "Re-run failed jobs" does not pick up workflow fixes merged later.
- Adoption depends on precise observation. An effect that landed differently (for example a conflicting existing tag) must fail closed, never be adopted.
- No local record of a failed run survives it; the providers are the record.
- Tag identity follows [ADR 9](0009-tag-identity-is-commit-and-annotation.md). Python version observation does not establish complete file-set publication; this is tracked in [the findings register](../projects/V1-FINDINGS.md).

## Enforcement

- `crates/callisto-cli/tests/release_hardening_tests.rs`: `p01_rerun_after_a_failed_publish_publishes_and_issues_a_receipt`, `p02_rerun_after_a_crate_is_already_published_completes_and_issues_a_receipt`, `p14_rerun_with_a_conflicting_existing_tag_fails_closed`.
- `crates/callisto-cli/tests/release_command_e2e_tests.rs`: `a_failed_run_writes_no_receipt_and_a_rerun_completes`.
- `crates/callisto-cli/tests/durable_release_e2e_tests.rs`: `newer_coordinator_executes_and_reruns_an_older_release_source`; rerun scenarios in `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release_simulator.rs`.
- `ReleaseExecutionStateV1` (`crates/callisto-model/src/release/execution.rs`) has no wire shape.

## Revisit when

- Release execution moves to an environment that keeps state between runs, and a provider cannot be observed well enough to adopt its effects.
- A provider offers no reliable way to tell "already landed as planned" from "landed differently".

## Sources

- PR #124 (592396564), commit bodies and PR body; closed PR #122
- PR #101 (279e32361): "reject incomplete quiescent execution", "accept an explicit recovery source"
- PR #39 (eeda4a2f5): durable attested execution
- Incident report §2, §6 (F-003), §8 (`git show 11038b11b^:.claude/plans/RELEASE-SELF-HOSTING-INCIDENT-2026-09-16.md`)
# 4. Ecosystem tools publish and own authentication

Status: Accepted (implemented in #143)

## Context

- Callisto releases to crates.io, npm, PyPI and GitHub. Each registry has its own auth rules, retries, rate limits and idempotence.
- The original design argued that `cargo` and `npm`/`pnpm` "already do registry auth, retries, rate-limit handling, and idempotence" (docs/00-design.md §9).

## Decision

Callisto decides what to publish and in what order, then runs the ecosystem tool as a subprocess through `CommandRunner`: `cargo`; `npm`, `pnpm`, `yarn` or `bun`; `python -m build` then `twine`; `gh`. The tool uses whatever credentials it finds and reports its own auth errors. Before each effect callisto observes provider state itself (`cargo info`, `npm view`, `curl` against the PyPI simple index, `gh api`, `git ls-remote`) and retries only those read-only observations (`retry_observation`, `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/provider/policy.rs`). Callisto links no HTTP client crate and runs no credential pre-flight.

## Options considered

- **Native registry clients in callisto** — rejected. The original design argued the tools "already do registry auth, retries, rate-limit handling, and idempotence — reimplementing any of that inside callisto would be redundant and would put callisto in the business of tracking every registry's quirks" (docs/00-design.md §9). §9.5 dropped `octocrab`/`reqwest`/`tokio` from the CLI, which "significantly shrinks the CLI's dependency surface".
- **Credential pre-flight before the first effect** — added in #134, removed in #143: "cargo, npm, twine and gh report their own auth failures, and a rerun adopts every effect that already landed, so a second credential model in Callisto only drifts from the tools'".

## Consequences

- Publishing uses each tool's native authentication. Observation must also reach the same destination: PyPI's curl read is not automatically authenticated by Twine's environment, and private-index route support needs an explicit boundary.
- A missing credential surfaces mid-release as E163 (E164 for `gh`), carrying the tool's redacted stderr. Effects before it have landed; a rerun adopts them (ADR 3).
- Callisto parses tool output to classify results (for example "already published"), so a tool's output change can break classification (`crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/registry_argv.rs`).
- Every release machine needs the tools on `PATH`.
- Read-only observation retries share a bounded policy, including transient command failures and Retry-After. Generated workflow auth setup and private Python observation routes remain tracked in [the findings register](../projects/V1-FINDINGS.md).

## Enforcement

- None automated. The fixed programs are in `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/provider/policy.rs` (`programs`: git, gh, cargo, npm, curl); the publish programs (pnpm, yarn, bun, `python3` or `python`, twine) are built in `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/registry_argv.rs`.
- No HTTP client crate (`reqwest`, `ureq`, `octocrab`, `hyper`) appears in `Cargo.lock`; nothing checks this.

## Revisit when

- A target registry has no CLI that can publish non-interactively.
- A tool's auth failure can leave a registry in a state a rerun cannot adopt.

## Sources

- docs/00-design.md §9, §9.5 (`git show 11038b11b^:docs/00-design.md`)
- PR #134 (3d0e2909d): pre-flight added and widened
- PR #143 (bde7305f9) "refactor!: let tools own auth; one build; lighter release and init", sub-commit "refactor(release)!: drop the local credential pre-flight"
# 8. Format-preserving manifest writes gated by ApplyPermit

Status: Accepted (implemented in 2c27f8d0b)

## Context

- Callisto rewrites files users own and review: `Cargo.toml`, `package.json`, `pyproject.toml`, changelogs, `pre.json`.
- `--dry-run` is a global flag; `release plan`, `release artifact-manifest` and `release execute` reject it (`crates/callisto-cli/src/error.rs`). "Respect `--dry-run`" was once a convention, and `pre enter`, `pre exit` and `init` forgot it: `pre` wrote `.changeset/pre.json` unconditionally (d15d4c2b0; `crates/callisto-model/src/permit.rs`).
- An interrupted run must never leave a partially written file (VER-APPLY-05, `docs/specs/versioning.json`).

## Decision

- TOML edits go through `toml_edit`, changing the existing item in place. `package.json` goes through `serde_json` with `preserve_order`, and indentation, line endings and BOM are detected on read and reproduced on write (`FormatFingerprint`). Callisto-owned JSON such as `pre.json` is regenerated canonically (`crates/callisto-model/src/format/pre.rs`).
- Every file content write goes through `callisto_model::atomic::atomic_write`: temp file in the target's directory, fsync, rename, then fsync the parent and grandparent. Deletions (consumed changesets, `pre.json`) and directory creation use `std::fs` directly.
- Write primitives take `&ApplyPermit`. Its only field is private; outside tests the only constructor is `ApplyPermit::granted_unless_dry_run(dry_run)`, which returns `None` on a dry run.

## Options considered

- **Parse into typed structs and serialize back (serde round-trip) for TOML** — reason not recorded. CM.4.1 only says editing the existing item in place, rather than replacing it, "is what makes `toml_edit` preserve comments, blank lines, key order, and inline-table formatting the caller did not touch" (docs/01-spec.md CM.4.1). JSON has no comments, so an order-preserving round trip plus fingerprint is enough (CM.5.1).
- **Regex or line-based edits** — reason not recorded. The rule appears in AGENTS.md invariant 2 without a stated reason.
- **Convention-based dry-run checks** — rejected: "A convention every new write site must remember will eventually be forgotten at one" (`permit.rs`), after `pre` and `init` did (d15d4c2b0). With a permit, a write site has nothing to pass unless its handler minted one (2c27f8d0b).

## Consequences

- TOML manifest diffs in release PRs show only version and dependency-spec changes. `package.json` is re-serialized with serde_json's pretty printer, keeping key order, indentation, line endings, BOM and trailing newline; other layout (for example an inline array) is normalized (`crates/callisto-manifests/src/npm.rs`).
- CRLF manifests and changelogs stay CRLF.
- A failed run can leave earlier files updated; `atomic_write` only prevents a torn single file (VER-APPLY-05).
- Tests need `ApplyPermit::force_for_tests()`, behind `cfg(test)` or the `callisto-model/test-util` feature, enabled only under `[dev-dependencies]`.
- The permit is a type check only. It does not stop code that calls `std::fs` directly, and a handler can still mint one with a literal `false`: `release`, `release artifact-manifest` and `init` do so behind their own dry-run branch (`crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/release.rs`, `init.rs`).

## Enforcement

- Type: `ApplyPermit` (`crates/callisto-model/src/permit.rs`), required by `atomic_write` (`crates/callisto-model/src/atomic.rs`), `Manifest::persist`, changelog writes and the release providers.
- Tests: `crates/callisto-cli/tests/dry_run_invariant_tests.rs` using `assert_no_disk_mutation` (`crates/callisto-fixtures/src/dry_run.rs`); format tests in `crates/callisto-manifests/src/cargo.rs` and `npm.rs` (CRLF, BOM, tab indent, comment and decor preservation).

## Revisit when

- A manifest format appears that no format-preserving editor supports.
- Writes must happen outside a command handler that can read the dry-run flag.

## Sources

- Commits 2c27f8d0b and d15d4c2b0 (ApplyPermit introduced; pre and init fixed)
- `crates/callisto-model/src/permit.rs` module docs; `crates/callisto-model/Cargo.toml` `test-util` comment
- `docs/specs/versioning.json` VER-APPLY-05
- docs/00-design.md §7.6 step 3; docs/01-spec.md CM.4.1, CM.5.1 (`git show 11038b11b^:docs/<file>`)
- Commit 435c05a17 (shared format fingerprint, CRLF fix)
# 9. A tag's identity is its commit and being annotated

Status: Proposed

## Context

- A rerun adopts effects that already landed (ADR 3), so it must decide whether an existing tag is the one it planned.
- The local check read the tag with `git for-each-ref` and compared the target commit and the annotation text. The remote check uses `git ls-remote`, which returns the tag object and peeled commit but not the annotation text, so it compared only the commit.
- The same repository state could therefore be adopted or rejected depending on whether the remote tag had been fetched.

## Decision

An existing tag is the planned tag when it names the planned commit and is annotated. Annotation text is not compared, locally or remotely. A lightweight tag or a tag on another commit is a conflict (E167) and is never adopted.

## Options considered

- **Compare the annotation text on both sides** — rejected: the remote side needs the tag object fetched first, and a tag created by a person or an earlier template would block every rerun.
- **Keep the split (text locally, commit remotely)** — rejected: the outcome depends on fetch state.

## Consequences

- Local and remote checks agree.
- A tag with a different message is adopted. The receipt records only the peeled commit (`ProviderEvidenceV1::GitTag { peeled_commit }` in `crates/callisto-model/src/release_observation.rs`), and `gh release create --verify-tag` checks only that the tag exists.

## Enforcement

- Tests in `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/provider/tag.rs` for local and remote observation (different annotation text is adopted; lightweight and other-commit tags conflict).
- REL-RERUN-02 and REL-RERUN-03 in `docs/specs/release.json`.

## Revisit when

- Something downstream starts reading the annotation text (release notes, signing policy, provenance).

## Sources

- Owner decision, `docs/projects/ROAD-TO-V1.md` "v1 fix plan" decisions (2026-09-25)
- The fix in this PR: "fix: stop comparing tag annotation text in release rerun observation"
# 11. Directory-keyed packages and promotion-aware history

Status: Accepted (implemented in #167)

## Context

- A package's id was its primary manifest name. When a second directory declared the same name in another ecosystem, walking promoted both to `cargo/foo` and `npm/foo` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/walk.rs`).
- Everything derived from the id changed with it. The default tag template was `{id}@{version}`, so an existing Cargo `foo` looked for `cargo/foo@*` tags, lost `foo@1.0.0`, and planned its next release from no prior tag.
- Selectors already tolerate promotion: `cargo/foo` resolves whether or not the package is promoted.

## Decision

- A package's stable identity is its workspace-relative directory: `Package::key() -> Option<PackageKey>` in `crates/callisto-model/src/package.rs`.
- `PackageId` is the display and selector form. Promotion changes how it prints (`foo` becomes `cargo/foo`), which bare selectors are ambiguous (E103), and the namespace of newly created default tags. The directory key and CHANGELOG path do not change.
- History recorded under a bare name follows the package that owned the name. Default tags are `{display id}@{version}` (`foo@1.0.0`, then `cargo/foo@1.1.0` once promoted), and a promoted package also finds `foo@*` tags whose commit contains its own manifest and no same-named package's. A bare `pre.json` key moves to the one same-named package that existed when `pre.json` was added. The CHANGELOG path comes from the directory.
- No configuration is needed. E101 is raised only when an explicit `tag-template` equals another package's default; E245 only when a bare `pre.json` key has no single owner.

## Options considered

- **Primary manifest name as key** — rejected: promotion changed the id, and with it the tag lookup of an already-released package.
- **Re-key every in-run map by `PackageKey`** — rejected for now: about 66 maps over roughly 1,000 `PackageId` uses. Promotion is computed once per walk, so within a run `PackageId` maps one-to-one onto `PackageKey`; re-keying would change no behavior.
- **Default tags from the native name (`foo@{version}`) for every package** — rejected: promoted `cargo/foo` and `npm/foo` would share tags, so one of them needed a `tag-template` (E101), and already-promoted workspaces would change their tag names.
- **Fall back to `{name}@` tags without an ownership check** — rejected: the newly added package would adopt the old one's releases.

## Consequences

- Adding a same-named package changes new default tag names, but does not rename existing tags or move the CHANGELOG. Historical bare tags and pre-release baselines are assigned through the ownership fallback; rename, manifest-roster and demotion gaps are tracked in [the findings register](../projects/V1-FINDINGS.md).
- Workspaces that are already promoted keep their `cargo/foo@*` tags unchanged.
- Ownership costs one `git rev-parse` per candidate tag of a promoted package.
- A pending changeset that names the bare `foo` is ambiguous after promotion (E103, WS-ID-06) and must be qualified.

## Enforcement

- `TagTemplate::default_for` in `crates/callisto-model/src/tag.rs`; the ownership fallback in `TagIndex::build` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/tags.rs`); `assign_promoted_pre_keys` in `crates/callisto-graph/src/lib.rs`.
- `promotion_changes_the_display_id_but_not_the_key` in `crates/callisto-graph/src/walk.rs`; `crates/callisto-cli/tests/identity_promotion_tests.rs`.
- WS-ID-03 and WS-ID-08 in `docs/specs/workspace.json`.

## Revisit when

- Something persists a package reference that is not a selector, tag or path, such as a cache keyed by package. It should use `PackageKey`.
- A package can move directories while keeping its identity.

## Sources

- Owner decision, `docs/projects/ROAD-TO-V1.md` "v1 fix plan" decisions (2026-09-25)
- #167 ("refactor(identity)!: key packages by directory; promotion is display-only") and its zero-config follow-up
# 12. Canonical distribution references and explicit release ownership

Status: Proposed

This proposal revises ADR 11's selector promotion and default-tag coupling when implemented. ADR 11 remains the current decision; it is not superseded by this documentation change.

## Context

The owner selected Rust/Cargo, npm/pnpm and Python/PyPI as the current scope, with architectural room for Go and .NET/NuGet. The system audit found that display promotion leaks into dependency rewrites, historical ownership and shared tag/forge ordering. Fresh Cargo/Maturin projects also fail because one package requires one grammar. Evidence and implementation work are recorded in [the findings register](../projects/V1-FINDINGS.md).

## Proposed decision

- Use canonical slash-qualified distribution references for new exact inputs, authored and generated data; reject new bare and colon-form aliases. Native normalization belongs to the ecosystem.
- Separate release ownership, distribution identity, authoritative version source and external effects. Reuse existing types and graphs; do not add a general plugin framework or opaque IDs without need.
- Read existing bare/colon references only through a deliberate compatibility/migration boundary with established ownership. Preserve historical tag ownership without using display promotion as a release-identity change.
- Keep native names and manifest context for dependency edits, inherited/derived versions and publisher arguments.
- Within Callisto's release-operation graph, shared external effects have one owner and wait for every required publication/output of that owner. For current ecosystems, public announcement follows registry completion; a future Go source tag can itself be publication.
- Native package-manager lifecycle hooks retain package-owner-defined behavior and environment. Callisto does not inspect, rewrite, suppress or reject hooks; effects initiated by owner-defined hooks are outside Callisto's release-operation graph.
- Reruns observe every required effect, including unfinished work after tag creation and missing Python files. Keep ADR 2's committed roster and ADR 3's no-journal recovery.

The exact owner representation, legacy-record migration, wire schema migration and channel/private-registry policies must be resolved in the relevant implementation change. This ADR does not approve those unspecified details or introduce release gates.

## Options considered

- Keep collision-triggered bare/qualified identity everywhere: retains inference rules at every new consumer and lets unrelated workspace changes alter identity behavior.
- Canonicalize one package ID but retain one grammar and per-distribution completion: does not represent Maturin version authority or shared tag/forge effects.
- Introduce a universal graph/plugin/build system: exceeds the supported use cases and duplicates ecosystem tools.

## Consequences

Pre-v1 breaking references are allowed by the owner requirement, but historical releases and committed decisions still need explicit compatibility. Cargo/npm/Python outputs can share an owner without pretending their native versions or registry evidence are interchangeable. Go/NuGet remain design examples, not shippe

# Road to v1

Unshipped work only. Baseline: main `07154021c` (0.10.2). [Owner requirement](../specs/REQ-DX-V1.md), [findings](V1-FINDINGS.md), [implementation and stacked-PR execution](V1-IMPLEMENTATION.md), [task definitions](V1-SYSTEM-HARDENING.json), [scoped model and prior art](../architecture/polyglot-v1.md).

## Scope and guardrails

- Rust/Cargo, npm/pnpm and Python/PyPI now, including concrete napi-rs and Cargo/Maturin layouts. Go and C#/.NET/NuGet are architecture examples only.
- Canonical native distribution references; deliberate legacy migration; separate release ownership and version authority.
- Reuse the dependency graph and operation DAG. Native dependency, build input and version coupling do not mean the same thing.
- Native tools/CI own building, packing and authentication. No universal package manager, build scheduler, public plugin platform, service graph or cross-registry transaction.
- Keep committed release authority and provider-observed recovery with no execution journal. Only execute receives registry secrets; no GitHub Environment or separate reviewer gate in this repo.
- Each implementation PR updates affected specs, tests and docs, with one changeset per independent user-facing topic. Future behavior is not inserted into current specs before its implementation.

## Sequence

The execution portfolio holds the remaining work as bounded units, including the D01 owner-contract checkpoint. The execution guide defines plugin routing, agent write ownership, serial Cargo verification and main-targeted stacked PRs under the existing CI trigger.

### 1. Correct the model in bounded changes

- D01: confirm exact ownership, compatibility, native authority and registry-output proof contracts before architectural code; existing-contract repairs do not wait for it.
- T06 and T06-HISTORY: canonical new references and legacy/history migration across selectors, config, groups, changesets, reports, pre-state and tags. Rename, manifest additions, promotion and demotion retain the right owner's history. [ADR 12](../adr/0012-canonical-distribution-release-ownership.md) remains proposed until implementation.
- T07: supported version authority and native distribution representations. Cover co-located Cargo/Maturin with Cargo-owned dynamic Python version and inspect built metadata; do not insert a second static version or build a universal converter.
- T08: shared physical effect ownership, so one tag, draft, upload or publication referenced by several distributions is executed once. The tag already waits for every registry publish of its package, and a rerun after a failed push completes the release. Retain the committed roster and no-journal executor. A future Go source tag is publication, not a universal completion marker.

The plan is an implementation portfolio, not an approved future-behavior spec. Resolve wire/compatibility choices and update the matching area spec with implementation; do not treat architectural packets as fully gated implementer handoffs before D01.

### 2. Reconcile generated workflows

The generated build-matrix workflow builds and places napi addons only for packages in the release intent. Native lifecycle hooks remain package-owner-defined and outside Callisto's release-operation graph; Callisto does not inspect or alter them.

A native Python argv test does not imply a generated Maturin workflow or authenticated private-index observation.

### 3. Verify supported workflows and onboarding

Each implementation unit adds its own regression/fault tests. T12 integrates these representative cases through production/native paths; T12-DX measures onboarding:

| Fixture | Evidence needed |
| --- | --- |
| Cargo workspace | Inherited/root versions, renamed dependencies, locked resolution and index propagation |
| npm/pnpm | Workspace ranges, aliases, paths, catalogs, peer/optional/private policy and packed metadata |
| Python | Native versions, extras/markers, prereleases, required wheel/sdist set and partial upload |
| Cargo+napi | Selected target builds, owner-defined lifecycle hooks preserved, Callisto-owned publication ordering and clean install/load |
| Cargo+Maturin | Co-located static/dynamic metadata, native version mapping and wheel metadata |
| Mixed workspace | No unrelated addon builds, foreign-name rewrites or missed affected lockfiles |
| History/retry | Correct ownership through transitions; missing push/forge/assets/files completed with original artifacts |

Retain local real-registry tests and record missing prerequisites as skips. Run `just ci` for implementation handoffs and workflow contract/policy checks for workflow changes. Measure fresh-repo first publication against the owner's ten-minute goal. Go/NuGet examples check model assumptions only; they are not new runtime gates.

## Owner decisions

- Canonical-reference compatibility, including colon form; source-owner representation and versioned wire migration.
- Authenticated private PyPI/HTML-only scope, npm channel policy, universal checksum requirements and wrapper bump severity.
- Inferred-only/manual releases: managed PR selection depends on changesets and verification requires a consumed changeset (ADR 2). Decide before broadening authorization.
- Build or drop a workspace-wide source-error-discard check; the Cargo lint is only a partial guard.
- Default tags for fixed/independent mode must be settled with canonical ownership, not a second tag-selection mechanism.
- Release-commit provenance: an unkeyed digest and decision/diff agreement do not prove which producer created the file. Decide whether existing authority is sufficient.
- Rust-cache pin in orin-dx/actions, bot-PR check policy and token rotation remain owner items.

## Other open work retained

- npm writes normalize arbitrary JSON layout; decide whether more than key order/indentation/line endings is needed.
- Preserve redacted stderr for indeterminate provider failures; never stream unredacted native-tool output.
- Publish final migration notices for retired callisto-format, callisto-vcs, callisto-conventional and callisto-changelog, naming callisto-model or callisto-graph.
- Evaluate rustc-provided target facts instead of the 18-triple table without making the core model Rust-target-specific.
- Require kind in explicit registry entries and attest napi .node outputs; define scope before adding a gate.
- Pin the floating moon minor in .prototools after checking proto compatibility.

## After 1.0 (additive)

- Effective-config explain from ConfigProvenance; remove redundant default-valued config afterward.
- .sha256 release-asset sidecars and proto verification.
- Glob fixed-group members.
- Auto-include README, LICENSE and CHANGELOG in release archives.
- Go/NuGet adapters and additional relationships only when concrete use cases and native tests justify them.
# V1 system findings

Baseline: main `07154021c` (0.10.2). This is an open findings register, not an implemented behavior spec: it lists unshipped defects and evidence gaps only. [Roadmap](ROAD-TO-V1.md), [execution guide](V1-IMPLEMENTATION.md), [task definitions](V1-SYSTEM-HARDENING.json), [proposed model](../architecture/polyglot-v1.md).

Confirmed means reproduced against the main binary or established by the cited code path; the evidence column distinguishes them. No hosted publication, competitor execution or fresh-repo timing run has been performed.

## Open confirmed defects

| Finding | Evidence and consequence | Plan | Contract/area |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SYS-MATURIN | `Package::version_grammar`: two fresh co-located Cargo/Maturin repos, with matching static versions and Cargo-owned dynamic Python versions, both reproduce E007 from init/status. Separate-directory fixtures did not cover this layout. | T07 | WS-ID-09; proposed version authority |

## Integration risks and evidence gaps

- Native npm lifecycle hooks can initiate effects outside Callisto's release-operation graph. Their behavior is package-owner-defined and is not inspected, rewritten, suppressed or rejected by Callisto; this is an explicit ownership boundary, not an automatic-enforcement defect.
- Registry version existence is not proof of identical package bytes or the desired npm dist-tag. A Python release is complete when every built file is on the index; the generated build-matrix workflow seals the file set in a credential-free build job and compares digests, while Python-only workspaces stay unsealed. Universal checksum enforcement and channel promotion remain owner decisions.
- Cargo and PyPI real local registry tests exist in `release_real_registry_e2e_tests.rs`; they drive publisher argv directly, bypass production binding/observation in those paths, and can skip when tools are missing. npm has broader end-to-end coverage. Record exercised versus skipped paths; do not mark the missing Cargo test as the remaining v1 blocker (T12).
- Fresh local Cargo/npm/PyPI repositories completed documented setup through release dry-run; npm packing and Cargo package inventory passed. Python artifact build was blocked on sandbox network access to `setuptools`, and no timings, credentials, registry publication or hosted release were exercised. The under-ten-minute first-published-release goal therefore remains unverified (T12-DX).
- Go v2/tag publication and NuGet normalized versions/RID/TFM assets are architecture examples only, not production support or new v1 gates (T07/T08/T12).

## Owner policy, not a defect verdict

Commit inference can produce pending bumps while `hasChangesets` is false; managed release-PR decisions then return noop. Committed verification also requires a consumed changeset, as ADR 2 states. 23	# 2. The committed version decision is the release authority
24	
25	Status: Accepted (implemented in #54)
26	
27	## Context
28	
29	- After the release PR merges, CI must verify the merged release commit before any publish, tag or GitHub release runs (PR #54).
30	- Before #54 the release roster was derived from the merged commit's raw diff and understood only a direct changeset-to-package match. It rejected any release in which a `[[fixed-group]]` cascade bumped a sibling that no changeset named (PR #54; code comment on `derive_release_commit_decision`).
31	
32	## Decision
33	
34	`callisto version --emit-decision <path>` writes the version decision it computed (package, target version, inclusion reasons) to `<path>`. The managed release-PR action writes it to `.callisto/release-decision.json` by default (`decision_path` input) and commits it in the release PR. After merge, `release plan --from-release-commit --decision <file>` reads that decision and confirms the merged commit's diff matches it exactly, no more and no less. CI never recomputes changeset, group or cascade policy at that boundary. The verified merge is also the authorization: the release workflow has no separate approval gate (no GitHub Environment approval or required reviewers) (incident report §2, requirements 1 and 2; PR #101, "fix(release): remove Environment approval gate").
35	
36	## Options considered
37	
38	- **Re-derive cascade and group policy in CI after merge, or keep the raw-diff roster and teach it about groups** — rejected. "Rather than teach the re-derivation about groups -- a second, incomplete reimplementation of changeset/group/cascade resolution -- this trusts the decision `callisto version` already computed and committed … One decision surface instead of two that can drift apart" (PR #54).
39	
40	## Consequences
41	
42	- The released roster and versions are exactly those committed in the release PR.
43	- The decision file is a wire contract. Its schema is versioned: `ReleaseDecisionV1::SCHEMA_VERSION` is 2, and the reader accepts 1 and 2 so an older release PR still plans (commit 7027bbfb0).
44	- A decision whose entries do not match its own digest fails to decode (E166) before the diff cross-check. The digest is an unkeyed SHA-256, not a signature, so an edit with a recomputed digest that still passes the decoder's roster checks is caught only by the diff cross-check.
45	- A release commit that does not add or modify the decision file, consumes no changeset, whose manifest versions disagree with the decision, or that leaves a claimed package's changelog untouched is refused (E165). Nothing checks that the decision file was produced by `callisto version --emit-decision`.
46	- `--emit-decision` derives and validates the decision before writes, then writes its file only after apply succeeds (`crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/version.rs`). A failed apply can leave earlier manifest writes without a decision; interrupted-command recovery is tracked separately.
47	
48	## Enforcement
49	
50	- `crates/callisto-cli/tests/durable_release_e2e_tests.rs`: `fixed_group_cascade_bump_without_direct_changeset_is_accepted`, `release_plan_rejects_a_commit_whose_manifest_disagrees_with_its_own_decision`, `release_plan_rejects_a_hand_tampered_decision_file`.
51	- `derive_release_commit_decision` in `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release_decision.rs` and its unit tests (head mismatch, corrupt decision file, claimed package not observed).

66	# 3. Reruns observe and adopt landed effects; no persisted execution state
67	
68	Status: Accepted (implemented in #124)
69	
70	## Context
71	
72	- A release is many external effects (registry publishes, tags, GitHub releases, asset uploads). Any run can die partway.
73	- Owner requirements: a merged but unpublished version must be recoverable without inventing a newer version; execution must fail unless every required operation reaches a verified terminal-success state; partial publication must be safely resumable from provider state (incident report §2, requirements 4, 7, 8).
74	- The same report proposed durably persisted execution state (§8, SPEC-RELEASE-EXECUTION-TERMINALITY criterion 3).
75	
76	## Decision
77	
78	Every run observes each operation's provider state immediately before that operation's effect and adopts an effect that already landed exactly as planned (a registry version already published is adopted with a warning); anything other than exact or absent stops the run (`execute_release`, `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release_execution.rs`). Execution state lives in memory for one run. A receipt is written only when every planned operation reached verified success; an incomplete run exits non-zero. An older merged release is recovered by a fresh run that plans it with `release plan --from-release-commit <sha> --decision <path> --orchestration-revision <current sha>`, not from a state file. Callisto's own release workflow exposes this as a `release_source_sha` dispatch input; workflows generated by `callisto init` do not (`crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/init.rs` tests).
79	
80	## Options considered
81	
82	- **Persisted execution state file with resume** — shipped in #39, proposed again in incident report §8, removed in #124: "CI never reads execution state back (every run is a fresh runner), yet an Initial run turned an already-published registry version into E174, so 'Re-run failed jobs' could never finish a partial release" (#124).
83	- **Recovery commands (`release reconcile`, `release execute --recovery`, `--state`) and Initial/Recovery run kinds** — rejected with the state file in #124. Removed with them: the workspace lock, `AdoptedExact`/`RecoveredExact`, E173, E174 and the release-state schema.
84	- **Rerun the historical workflow run to recover** — rejected. A rerun of an old GitHub Actions run does not pick up workflow fixes merged later (incident report §2 requirement 6; §6 F-003).
85	- **Post-publish re-observation pass to build the receipt** — rejected: a flaky registry read could fail a release whose effects had all landed (#122, #124).
86	
87	## Consequences
88	
89	- A rerun ("Re-run failed jobs" or a fresh run on the release commit) finishes a partial release whose remaining operations can now succeed; "Re-run failed jobs" does not pick up workflow fixes merged later.
90	- Adoption depends on precise observation. An effect that landed differently (for example a conflicting existing tag) must fail closed, never be adopted.
91	- No local record of a failed run survives it; the providers are the record.
92	- Tag identity follows [ADR 9](0009-tag-identity-is-commit-and-annotation.md). Python version observation does not establish complete file-set publication; this is tracked in [the findings register](../projects/V1-FINDINGS.md).
93	
94	## Enforcement
95	
96	- `crates/callisto-cli/tests/release_hardening_tests.rs`: `p01_rerun_after_a_failed_publish_publishes_and_issues_a_receipt`, `p02_rerun_after_a_crate_is_already_published_completes_and_issues_a_receipt`, `p14_rerun_with_a_conflicting_existing_tag_fails_closed`.
97	- `crates/callisto-cli/tests/release_command_e2e_tests.rs`: `a_failed_run_writes_no_receipt_and_a_rerun_completes`.
98	- `crates/callisto-cli/tests/durable_release_e2e_tests.rs`: `newer_coordinator_executes_and_reruns_an_older_release_source`; rerun scenarios in `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release_simulator.rs`.
99	- `ReleaseExecutionStateV1` (`crates/callisto-model/src/release/execution.rs`) has no wire shape.
100	
101	## Revisit when
102	
103	- Release execution moves to an environment that keeps state between runs, and a provider cannot be observed well enough to adopt its effects.
104	- A provider offers no reliable way to tell "already landed as planned" from "landed differently".
105
